{{nihongo|'''Ikamashi Shrine'''|伊加麻志神社}} is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945}} located in Horigiri, {{ill|Izu, Shizuoka|Q696840|qid=Q696840}}, {{ill|Shizuoka Prefecture|Q131320|qid=Q131320}}.<ref>[http://www.shizuoka-jinjacho.or.jp/shokai/jinja.php?id=4402194 Ikamashi Shrine] - Shizuoka Prefecture Association of Shinto Shrines</ref> {{nihongo|'''Ikamashi Shrine'''|伊加麻志神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Izu Province]].

== Overview ==
It is enshrined within the precincts of Masuyamadera Temple, located atop Mt. Masuyama, between {{ill|Mount Katsuragi|Q11620896|qid=Q11620896|lt=Mount Katsuragi}} and {{ill|Mount Jō|Q11426081|qid=Q11426081|lt=Mount Shiro}} and {{ill|Mount Hottanjō|Q11579067|qid=Q11579067}} (the so-called Izu Three Mountains), at the northern edge of the Horigiri district in northwestern Izu City.<ref>[https://kanko.city.izu.shizuoka.jp/form1.html?c1=7&c2=8&pid=3185 Masuyamadera Temple] - Izu City</ref>

Although the date of foundation is unknown, it is identified with the {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}} of the same name, Ikamashi Shrine, and is an ancient shrine recorded in the {{ill|Izu Province Shinkaichō|Q17193087|qid=Q17193087}} as “Junior Fourth Rank Upper, Takayama no Myōjin.”<ref name="gen">[https://genbu.net/data/izu/ikamasi_title.htm Ikamashi Shrine] - Genmatsuko</ref><ref name="engi">[http://engishiki.org/izu/bun/iz140209-01.html Ikamashi Shrine] - Research on Engishiki Shrines</ref>

From the Edo period until the early Meiji period, it was called Mishima Myōjin (Mishima Shrine).<ref name="gen"/><ref name="engi"/>
